content.text:
Catalog search now ignores accents, so `garcia marquez` finds García Márquez. It works the other way too: an accented query matches unaccented titles. All 61 tests pass, including the new one.

The fix is in `normaliseText` in `lib/helpers/text.js`. It now splits accented letters into base letter plus accent and drops the accent marks before lowercasing. `searchCatalog` runs both the query and the title and author through that function, so nothing changed in `lib/catalog/search.js`. Search was the only caller, so nothing else is affected.

I added a test in `test/catalog.test.js` covering `garcia marquez`, `GARCÍA MÁRQUEZ`, `anos` matching "años", and the decomposed (combining-accent) form of "García".

Two limits:
- Letters that aren't a base letter plus an accent, such as `ł`, `ø` and `ß`, are not folded. `lodz` won't match `Łódź`.
- Result sorting still uses `localeCompare`, which I left as it was.

One of my shell commands was blocked by a permission check, so I made the edits with the file-edit tool instead. Nothing was left half-applied.
